QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_30

question.text: A futures seller's contract settles at Rs 4,50,000. The applicable STT rate for equity futures is 0.02% on the sell side. What is the STT payable?

answer.text: Rs 90 (0.02% x Rs 4,50,000 = Rs 90, paid by the seller)
Rs 562.50 (0.125% x Rs 4,50,000 — using the exercised-option STT rate)
Rs 450 (0.10% x Rs 4,50,000 — using the option-sale STT rate on premium)
Rs 180 (0.02% x Rs 4,50,000 paid by both buyer and seller = Rs 90 x 2)

explanation.text: The Logic: STT on equity futures is 0.02% of the transaction value, payable by the SELLER only. On Rs 4,50,000: STT = 0.02% x 4,50,000 = Rs 90. The Trap: STT on futures is paid only by the seller, not both parties. The current equity option STT rates are 0.10% on the seller on the option premium for a sale of an option, and 0.125% on the purchaser on the settlement price when an option is exercised — neither of these applies to a futures settlement. Note: STT is levied only on equity derivatives. Currency derivatives and interest rate derivatives are currently not subject to STT. Across equity derivatives, the rates are: futures sale 0.02% on traded value, option sale 0.10% on premium, exercised option 0.125% on settlement price.
